QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_33

question.text: An NPO must be registered under which Section of the Income Tax Act 1961 to qualify for current tax-exempt status, and under which Section can it extend tax deduction to its donors?

answer.text: Section 80C for the NPO; Section 80G for the donor.
Section 12AB for the NPO's current tax-exempt status (with 12A/12AA as the prior/legacy regime); Section 80G for the donor's deduction on donation.
Section 10 for the NPO; Section 24 for the donor.
Section 139 for the NPO; Section 56 for the donor.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p.215 (Chapter 10), all NPOs must be registered under Section 12AB of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for tax-exempt status; p.217 explains 12AB registration and its validity. Donor-side deduction continues to flow through Section 80G. p.55 references Section 12A as the legacy regime, but 12AB is the current requirement post-Finance Act 2020. The Trap: Option A confuses 80C (individual savings deduction) with the NPO side. Option C invents wrong Sections. Option D confuses filing Section 139 with registration status. Note: Lead with 12AB for current status; treat 12A/12AA only as prior/legacy context. Retain Section 80G as the donor deduction route.
